questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.
Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic going straight. You must always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: When stopped for a traffic violation, what must you show a police officer?

options.text: Only your insurance and registration.
Only your license.
Your license, insurance, and registration.

questions.explanation: You must have your license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance ready. You need all three documents whenever you drive.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Winding road ahead.
Do not enter.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road curves ahead.

questions.question: A truck or bus is turning right where you also need to turn right. What should you do?

options.text: Turn quickly before the truck or bus does.
Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning before you turn.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning before you turn.
questions.explanation: Do not try to fit your vehicle between a turning truck or bus and the curb. This can cause a serious crash. Wait for the truck or bus to complete its turn before you turn.

questions.question: What does a steady green traffic light mean?

options.text: Speed up.
Adjust your mirrors.
You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if the path is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if the path is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can proceed through the intersection. First check that no other traffic or pedestrians are in your way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right turn.
Intersection ahead.
Lane change.

questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that your road meets another road straight ahead. Slow down and be ready to yield or stop before turning.

questions.question: In rain or fog, which headlights should you use to see better?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, or fog. High beams reflect off the water or fog and shine back in your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
One-way.
Stop.

questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop at this sign.

questions.question: When must you yield to a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog?

options.text: Only when the guide dog is leading the person across the street.
At all times.
Only if a crossing guard is present.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians with guide dogs or white canes have the right-of-way at all times. You must always yield to them.

questions.question: What is a driving distraction?

options.text: Anything that makes you take evasive action while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you pay more attention to driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your focus off driving. Distractions can happen anywhere and anytime. They can cause crashes, injuries, and death.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
You must turn right.
Watch for traffic on your right.

questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this location.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. You should:

options.text: Sound your horn and maintain your speed.
Speed up to clear the area quickly.
Slow down and pass with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pass with caution.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you see pedestrians near the road. Be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: Children on bicycles should be given extra space by drivers because:

options.text: They do not have the same reflexes as adults.
They are smaller and harder to see.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Look carefully for children near schools, parks, and playgrounds. Watch for children on bikes who may suddenly enter the road.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross after the "Don't Walk" signal flashes. They are in the middle of the street when your light turns green. You should:

options.text: Proceed if you have the right-of-way.
Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
Wait until the pedestrian crosses the street before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the pedestrian crosses the street before proceeding.
questions.explanation: At a green light, give the right-of-way to anyone in the intersection. Wait for all pedestrians to cross before you move.

questions.question: In a vehicle with airbags, where is the safest place for children age 12 and under to sit?

options.text: The front seat.
The back seat.
The bed of a pick-up truck.

questions.explanation: Children age 12 and under should sit in the back seat. Airbags can hurt children in the front seat.

questions.question: What do "No passing zone" signs tell drivers?

options.text: To speed up slightly.
That it is not safe to pass.
To maintain a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: That it is not safe to pass.
questions.explanation: "No passing zone" signs mean it is not safe to pass another vehicle. The road ahead has poor visibility.

questions.question: When you see a person crossing with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until the person is well away from your path.
Honk your horn as you drive past them.
Carefully drive around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is well away from your path.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, stop and let them cross. Always give blind pedestrians the right-of-way.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?

options.text: Before you start driving.
Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before you start driving. Also adjust your seat and fasten your safety belt. Do not adjust mirrors while moving.

questions.question: You should use your horn:

options.text: Whenever it may help prevent a collision.
To get other drivers moving in traffic.
When you are angry with another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever it may help prevent a collision.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to get another driver's attention if it will help prevent a crash.

questions.question: What is an important step when turning?

options.text: Check traffic in all directions.
Increase your speed.
Always move to the left lane.

questions.explanation: Before turning, look to the rear and both sides of your vehicle to make sure it is safe. Slow down to safely complete the turn.

questions.question: You see a pedestrian crossing your lane. There is no crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact and then pass the pedestrian.
Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians in any crosswalk, marked or unmarked. Even without a crosswalk, always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: How can you identify an aggressive driver?

options.text: They make erratic or improper lane changes.
The number of passengers in their car.
They drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make erratic or improper lane changes.
questions.explanation: Watch other drivers around you. If you see a driver making erratic or improper lane changes, they may be aggressive. Do not challenge them. The safest action is to stay away from them.

questions.question: After drinking several beers, the effects of alcohol will only decrease by:

options.text: Taking a cold shower.
Waiting several hours.
Drinking several cups of coffee.

questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee, exercise, or cold showers do not speed this up. It takes about one hour for your body to process one drink.

questions.question: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver:

options.text: Relax and focus on driving.
Drive above the posted speed limit.
Tailgate the driver in front of you.

questions.explanation: Focus on driving and do not take other drivers' actions personally. Allow extra time for your trip, follow speed limits, and be patient with other drivers.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Turn up your radio volume.
Pull into a safe parking area and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull into a safe parking area and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs of fatigue: struggling to keep your eyes open, drifting from your lane, or turning up the radio to stay awake. If you notice these signs, find a safe place to park and rest with a short nap.
